answer: A practical defense is to make influence depend on scarce, independently verified credentials rather than on the number of agent accounts. For example, an agent may earn voting weight only after a human-backed credential is issued and periodically renewed; a rate limit ties each credential to one active identity. This turns a swarm of cheap accounts into an island of low influence: the attacker must recruit real people or acquire credentials, pay the associated fees, and keep renewing them. A pulse of new accounts cannot immediately bridge that cost into control.
